articles.summary: A bank or IMB that owns servicing rights and outsources the work keeps the regulatory liability, and most oversight programs still run on the subservicer's own scorecard, an annual audit and a sampled call file. What changes when the owner can score every call and every letter against Regulation X, Regulation F, UDAAP and its own procedures, what the contract has to say first, and what we learned codifying hundreds of SOP documents for a lender's call review.
articles.title: Your Subservicer's Calls Become Your Exam Findings: Overseeing a Mortgage Subservicer When You Can Review Every Call and Letter

articles.summary: An initial, extended or active duty alert on a tri-merge report restricts the lender by statute, and the verification has to go to the phone number in the alert, which is not always the one on the application. Address discrepancy notices carry their own duty under Regulation V. A technical account of how our agents read alerts on every credit pull, what they compare, and why we decided the verification call is made by a person.
articles.title: A Fraud Alert on the Credit Report Is a Legal Stop: What FCRA Section 605A Requires Before a Mortgage Proceeds, and Who Makes the Call

articles.summary: Title and hazard insurance arrive from third parties, late in the process, and get a glance because someone else is responsible for them. Then the vesting does not match the note, the mortgagee clause names the wrong entity, or the deductible exceeds the investor limit, and the defect is found after funding. A technical account of the cross-document checks our pre-close QC agent runs on these two documents, the Fannie Mae B7-2 and B7-3 rules behind them, and where the TRID and fraud checks meet them.
articles.title: The Title Commitment and the Insurance Declaration: What Pre-Close QC Has to Check Against the Rest of the File

articles.summary: A rate move puts thousands of loans in the money in the same week, and the servicer has the data to reach those borrowers first. Before an AI agent dials any of them, it has to know which loans can actually close: VA's seasoning and recoupment tests under 38 U.S.C. 3709, the early payoff window on loans you sold, which consent covers a marketing call, and what the agent may and may not say about savings. What we learned running a voice agent on a lender's funnel, applied to the recapture campaign.
articles.title: When Rates Drop, Your Servicing Portfolio Gets Called by Someone: Refinance Recapture With an AI Voice Agent, and the Tests That Decide Who It Calls

articles.summary: The same monthly benefit produces a different qualifying income under Fannie Mae, FHA and VA, and the gross-up is applied to the whole check far more often than the rules allow. A technical account of how our income agent reads the taxable fraction off the tax return, reconciles the award letter against the deposit, tests continuance from documented terms rather than age, and where Regulation B draws the line on what an underwriter may ask.
articles.title: Social Security, Pensions and the Gross-Up: Calculating Nontaxable and Retirement Income Without Counting It Twice

articles.summary: Variable income is where qualifying figures go wrong quietly: a March bonus annualized over nine months, overtime averaged across a decline, a written VOE that lumps earning types together. A technical account of how our income agent separates earning types, picks the averaging period, handles a declining trend, and cites the rule, written after Fannie Mae's March 2026 reorganization moved bonus and overtime policy from B3-3.1-03 to B3-3.3-02.
articles.title: Overtime, Bonus and Commission: The Trending Math an AI Income Agent Has to Get Right, and Where Fannie Mae Moved the Rules in 2026

articles.summary: A foreclosure referral sent a week early, or while a complete loss mitigation application sat unreviewed, is the kind of Regulation X violation that shows up in a borrower's lawsuit before it shows up in an exam. The checks behind the 120-day rule in 12 CFR 1024.41(f), the dual-tracking limits in 1024.41(g), the SCRA and bankruptcy holds, and state pre-foreclosure notices, and why we re-run every one of them on the day the first notice is filed, not only the day the file is referred.
articles.title: The Day Before the Foreclosure Referral: What a Default Desk Has to Prove, and Prove Again on the Day Counsel Files

articles.summary: Mortgage operations already run on maker-checker: the underwriter decides, QC re-checks, a manager signs the exception. An AI agent that writes to the system of record should be held to the same separation, and a single model with a self-reported confidence score is not that. A technical account of how our three verification layers are built, what the checker is and is not allowed to see, why disagreements are never settled by a vote, and how the auto-clear threshold gets set.
articles.title: Maker, Checker, Threshold: Why a Mortgage AI Agent Gets Three Independent Chances to Say No Before It Writes to the LOS

articles.summary: Most mortgage defects are not created in underwriting or closing. They enter the file in the first days, as a missing page, a stale paystub or a figure that disagrees with its source, and they get more expensive at every stage they survive. An account of what a clean file actually means, why quality keeps getting pushed downstream to the most expensive people in the operation, and how our agents move the checks to the moment a document arrives.
articles.title: The Clean File: Why the Strongest Mortgage Operations Build Quality In at Intake, Not at QC

articles.summary: By the time a defaulted loan reaches the claim, every mistake made since the first missed payment shows up as a number someone deducts. A claim package is hundreds of pages of servicing history, invoices and legal fees that have to agree with each other, and FHA's curtailment rules punish the dates that do not. What we learned running a claims agent in production for a post-default claims outsourcer, where it helps, and why a specialist still files.
articles.title: Curtailment Is Written Against Dates: Preparing FHA and Mortgage Insurance Claims With an AI Agent in Post-Default Servicing

articles.summary: Calling a web lead back in under a minute is the easy part. Doing it inside federal and state calling hours, on consent you can prove, without the agent drifting into loan-originator activity or qualifying the 9pm lead differently from the 9am one, is where speed-to-lead programs get into trouble. What we learned putting a voice agent on both ends of a top-25 IMB's funnel, including the 9.2x jump in booked appointments and what it did to the loan officers' calendars.
articles.title: The Mortgage Lead That Arrives at 9pm on a Sunday: Speed-to-Lead With an AI Voice Agent, and the Lines It Does Not Cross

articles.summary: A servicemember's Leave and Earnings Statement carries taxable base pay, nontaxable allowances that depend on duty station and dependents, allotments that can reveal debts the credit report does not show, and an expiration of term of service date that decides whether the income continues. A technical account of what our income agent reads from an LES, how it handles a PCS move and an ETS inside twelve months, and how VA's residual income test in 38 CFR 36.4340 is computed and cited.
articles.title: Reading a Leave and Earnings Statement Like an Underwriter: Military Income, the ETS Date and VA Residual Income for an AI Income Agent

articles.summary: Every credit document in a mortgage file has an age limit, and the limit is measured against a date nobody knows when the document arrives: the note date, or for FHA the disbursement date. When closing slips, documents that were fine go stale, and the file finds out at funding. A technical account of how our agents read each document's effective date, keep an expiry calendar against a closing date that moves, and request the refresh before the window shuts.
articles.title: The Paystub Was Current on Day 3: Tracking Document Age on a Mortgage File That Runs Longer Than Planned

articles.summary: Whether a mortgage is a higher-priced mortgage loan under Regulation Z 1026.35 depends on the APR, the average prime offer rate for the week the rate was set, and the loan's lien and size. A relock, a pricing exception or a fee change can move a loan across the line after the escrow waiver and the appraisal order were already decided. A technical account of how our agents compute HPML status, when they re-test it, and the escrow, appraisal and flipped-property consequences they check before closing.
articles.title: A Loan Can Become Higher-Priced After It Is Locked: Re-Testing HPML Status at Every Change, and What Follows When It Flips

articles.summary: SAVE is gone, RAP has a $10 floor, and millions of credit reports still show a student loan payment that no longer exists. A technical account of how an underwriting agent reconciles every liability across the 1003, the tri-merge and the documents, why the same borrower carries a different DTI under Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and FHA, and why we let the agent add a debt on its own but never remove one.
articles.title: The Student Loan Payment on the Credit Report Is Probably Stale: Liabilities, DTI and What an Underwriting Agent Has to Reconcile After SAVE

articles.summary: Regulation B requires evidence, at the time of application, that each co-applicant intended to apply jointly, and it bars a creditor from requiring a spouse's signature on the note when the applicant qualifies alone. Both rules are old, both are among the findings examiners write most often, and both get harder when the application is a conversation instead of a form. How we capture joint intent at the point of sale, why it is a separate event from the accuracy attestation, and what the agent is not allowed to suggest.
articles.title: Who Is Actually Applying? Joint Intent, Co-Applicants and Spousal Signatures When an AI Agent Runs the Mortgage Application
